texts.facts: 4. The facts of the case are that the Food Inspector collected the sample of mixed milk on 12.07.2001 at 10.15 a.m. after purchase it from the revisionist. The same was then filled in three bottles and sent them for analysis before the Public Analyst who vide his report dated 10.8.2001 found milk fat to be 7.2% whereas milk solid not fat to be 7.8%. 5. In the present case the Food Analyst has reported that the mixed milk is deficient by 8% of milk solid not fat which is an incorrect report since milk solid not fat was found to be 7.8 % whereas the standard prescribed as per the rules is 8.5%. The revisionist was charged vide order dated 18.12.2009 by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Kanshi Ram Nagar for offence under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act for breach of rule. 6. In the trial Food Inspector was examined as P.W.1 under Section 244 Cr.P.C. after which no witness was examined and Kanhaiya Lal and Anil Kumar Bhardwaj were examined as P.W.2 and 3 respectively under Section 246 Cr.P.C. 7. The accused while giving his statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. denied the charges levelled against him. No defence evidence was led. A complaint was filed by the Food Inspector against the revisionist for offences under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 before the court concerned on which cognizance was taken and the applicant was tried. He has been extended benefit of set of under Section 428 Cr.P.C. The fine and default clause remained same. The present revision has thus been filed.
texts.arguments: 9. Learned counsel for the revisionist argued that the prosecution against the revisionist was drawn on an incorrect finding of the Public Analyst inasmuch as the prescribed standard of milk solid not fat is 8.5% whereas the same was found to be 7.8% but the report stated it to be deficient by 8%. There is no evidence whatsoever to show that the said milk was first stired and then sample was taken. The fat in the milk gets settled being heavy and as such the same needs to be stired before Surendra Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53100146/ 2 taking the sample. It is argued that the complainant has not stated in his statement that he did stir the milk and then took the sample of the same. Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and arguments and argued that the trial court has given cogent reasons for convicting the revisionist.
